## 2026-07-22 01:45 UTC -- #77 PR #128: addressed review comment (graceful-shutdown row release) (sweep)

Operator review on draft PR #128 asked for one change: release the singleton `instance` row on graceful shutdown, otherwise a same-second restart hits our own still-fresh heartbeat and refuses to boot (turning CUSTODE_TAKEOVER into the front door).

Implemented on branch fix/77-single-instance-guard:
- `Process.flag(:trap_exit, true)` in `init/1` so a supervisor `:shutdown` runs terminate instead of an outright kill.
- `terminate/2` deletes the row when we still hold it, guarded on `os_pid == ours` so a takeover victim never deletes its usurper's row. Crash paths still rely on staleness.
- Stored resolved `os_pid` in GenServer state for the guard.
- Two regression tests: graceful stop → holder nil → fresh claim succeeds immediately; and takeover-victim stop leaves the usurper's row untouched.

All 5 CI gates green locally (format, compile --warnings-as-errors, credo --strict, test). 189 tests pass (was 187). Committed 66b3e4b, pushed to same branch. PR stays draft awaiting human review/ready/merge.

## 2026-07-22 01:40 UTC -- #77 implemented: single-instance heartbeat guard -> draft PR #128 (sweep)

Approved gate implemented in worktree on branch fix/77-single-instance-guard (off fresh origin/main).

What landed:
- Migration 20260721000007_add_instance_heartbeat: singleton `instance` table (key, node, os_pid, beat_at).
- lib/custode/instance.ex: Custode.Instance GenServer. claim/2 checks the row before Oban starts; refuses to boot (init -> {:stop, {:instance_conflict, holder}}) when a fresh foreign heartbeat exists; reclaims free/stale/own rows; CUSTODE_TAKEOVER=1 (or app env :instance_takeover) seizes regardless. Beats every 10s, staleness window 30s. os_pid (System.pid()) is the per-boot identity since node is always nonode@nohost.
- Wired into application.ex between the Ecto.Migrator and Oban so the refusal happens before any polling.
- test/custode/instance_test.exs: 8 tests (claim outcomes + guard boot path). Added `instance` to the test_helper truncate list.

All 5 CI gates green locally: format, compile --warnings-as-errors, credo --strict, full test suite 187 passed. Pushed, draft PR #128 opened via repo_open_pr, plan posted on the issue via repo_mark_issue_ready.

Scope note in PR: this is issue option 2a (heartbeat). Option 3 (stop Oban first on shutdown) left out to keep the guard self-contained; a possible follow-up. Draft left as draft (approved action said open a draft PR, not mark ready) -- awaiting human review/CI.

## 2026-07-22 00:45 UTC -- #7 confirmed: config drift on cron tick args (sweep)

Explore agent confirmed the issue is real: Routine.crontab/1 (lib/custode/routine.ex:68-83) bakes tick_args(routine) statically into Oban's crontab list at Application.start (lib/custode/application.ex:60-70); Oban's Cron plugin re-fires stored args forever, never recomputing. Custode.beat/0 (lib/custode.ex:37) already rebuilds args live -- that's the manual path that works. Fix is small: add lib/custode/routine_tick.ex, a thin Oban worker taking %{"routine_id" => id} that does Routine.get(id) |> Routine.tick_args() |> ObanClaude.Agent.Tick.new() |> Oban.insert(), then point the crontab entry at it with minimal args instead of baking tick_args directly. ~1-2 files, ~20 lines, no changes to application.ex or oban_claude dep. Proposing as this sweep's gate.
